mai.title: स्त्रीवादी दर्शनक अनेक स्वर
mai.summary: स्त्रीवादी दर्शन एक सिद्धान्त नहि, बहुध्वनिक दार्शनिक क्षेत्र अछि। ओकर साझा प्रेरणा (gendered oppression), (exclusion) आ (unequal power)क आलोचना हो सकैत अछि, मुदा (equality), (difference), (body), (sexuality), (care), (knowledge), (identity) आ (emancipation) पर उत्तर विविध अछि। उदारवादी (feminism) अधिकार आ (equal citizenship)क शक्तिशाली भाषा देलक; (radical feminism sexuality/family/power)क गहिर संरचना देखलक; (socialist feminism labour), (reproduction) आ (economy) जोड़लक; (care ethics dependency) आ (relation)क नैतिक महत्व समक्ष आनलक।

en.title: The Many Voices of Feminist Philosophy
en.summary: Feminist philosophy is not a single doctrine but a polyphonic philosophical field. Its shared inspiration may be criticism of gendered oppression, exclusion and unequal power, yet its answers concerning equality, difference, body, sexuality, care, knowledge, identity and emancipation are diverse. Liberal feminism supplied a powerful language of rights and equal citizenship; radical feminism exposed deeper structures of sexuality, family and power; socialist feminism joined labour, reproduction and economy; care ethics brought the moral importance of dependency and relation to the foreground.

mai.title: सिमोन द बोउवार: स्त्री बनाओल जाइत अछि
mai.summary: सिमोन द बोउवारक दर्शनक स्थायी शक्ति एहि बातमे अछि जे ओ ‘स्त्री’ केँ (fixed essence) नहि, (situated becoming) रूपमे पढ़ैत अछि। एहि सँ (biology), (society) आ (agency)क बीच सरल (either/or) टूटैत अछि। (The Second Sex) क (Other thesis) देखबैत अछि जे (domination)केँ बुझबा लेल (explicit hostility) मात्र नहि, (universal norm)क निर्माण सेहो जाँचबाक पड़त।

en.title: Simone de Beauvoir: Woman Is Made
en.summary: The enduring strength of Simone de Beauvoir’s philosophy lies in reading ‘woman’ not as a fixed essence but as situated becoming. This breaks the simple either/or between biology, society and agency. The Other thesis of The Second Sex shows that understanding domination requires examination not only of explicit hostility but also of the construction of the universal norm.

mai.title: देह, अनुभव आ सत्ता
mai.summary: देह, अनुभव आ सत्ता सम्बन्धी (feminist) दर्शनक मुख्य योगदान ई अछि जे ओ शरीरकेँ मनक अधीन वस्तु नहि, (world-engaged subject) मानैत अछि। (perception), (movement), (habit) आ (affect) दार्शनिक विषय बनैत छथि। अनुभव शुद्ध (private) तथ्य नहि, मुदा निरर्थक सेहो नहि।

en.title: Body, Experience and Power
en.summary: The principal contribution of feminist philosophy concerning body, experience and power is to treat the body not as an object subordinate to the mind but as a world-engaged subject. Perception, movement, habit and affect thereby become philosophical subjects. Experience is not a pure private fact, but neither is it meaningless.

mai.title: जूडिथ बटलर: लिंग (gender), प्रदर्शनात्मकता (performativity) आ पहचान
mai.summary: जूडिथ बटलरक स्थायी योगदान ई जे (gender) केँ स्थिर (property) सँ प्रक्रिया दिस मोड़ि देलनि। (Gender) “अछि” मात्र नहि; सामाजिक पुनरावृत्ति, सम्बोधन, (norm) आ (institution)क माध्यमसँ “बनैत” रहैत अछि। (Performativity)क अर्थ (theatrical choice) नहि।

en.title: Judith Butler: Gender, Performativity and Identity
en.summary: Judith Butler’s enduring contribution is to shift gender from a fixed property toward a process. Gender does not merely ‘exist’; it is continually ‘made’ through social repetition, forms of address, norms and institutions. Performativity does not mean theatrical choice.

mai.title: अन्तर्संबद्ध असमानता (intersectionality): जाति, वर्ग, लिंग, धर्म आ क्षेत्र
mai.summary: (Intersectionality)क ऐतिहासिक महत्व ई अछि जे ओ (single-axis) न्याय-दृष्टिक (blind spot) स्पष्ट करैत अछि। कोनो व्यक्ति जखन अनेक सत्ता-संरचनाक (crossing point) पर अछि, तखन ओकर अनुभव केवल एक (category)क (representative case) नहि रहैत। किम्बर्ले क्रेंशॉक योगदान (additive discrimination)क भाषा केँ (structural), (political) आ (representational intersectionality) दिस मोड़ैत अछि।

en.title: Intersectional Inequality: Caste, Class, Gender, Religion and Region
en.summary: The historical importance of intersectionality lies in making visible the blind spots of single-axis views of justice. When a person stands at the crossing point of several structures of power, that person’s experience is no longer merely a representative case of one category. Kimberlé Crenshaw’s contribution shifts the language of additive discrimination toward structural, political and representational intersectionality.

mai.title: भारतीय स्त्रीवादी दर्शनक प्रश्न
mai.summary: भारतीय स्त्रीवादी दर्शनक मुख्य उपलब्धि ई अछि जे ओ (gender) प्रश्नकेँ परिवारक निजी मामला सँ निकालि जाति, वर्ग, धर्म, राष्ट्र, कानून, श्रम, ज्ञान, शरीर, भाषा आ पर्यावरणक व्यापक संरचनासँ जोड़ैत अछि। एकर इतिहास (colonial modernity) आ (indigenous reform)क सरल द्वन्द्व नहि। भारतीय महिलासभ स्वयं लेखन, शिक्षा, (anti-caste) संघर्ष, राष्ट्रवादी आन्दोलन, (labour politics), कानून आ साहित्यक माध्यमसँ (theory) बनौलनि।

en.title: Questions of Indian Feminist Philosophy
en.summary: The central achievement of Indian feminist philosophy is that it takes gender out of the category of a private family matter and connects it with the wider structures of caste, class, religion, nation, law, labour, knowledge, body, language and environment. Its history is not a simple opposition between colonial modernity and indigenous reform. Indian women themselves produced theory through writing, education, anti-caste struggle, nationalist movements, labour politics, law and literature.

mai.title: मिथिलाक समानान्तर स्त्री-दृष्टि
mai.summary: मिथिलाक समानान्तर स्त्री-दृष्टि कोनो पुरातन गौरवक घोषणा नहि, वरन् (method) अछि—स्थानिक स्रोत सुनू, संस्थाक सत्ता जाँचू, अनुभव केँ (essentialize) नहि करू, आ न्यायिक कसौटी स्पष्ट राखू। एहि दृष्टिमे पाँजी, विवाह, परिवार, गीत, कला, श्रम, प्रवासन, बाढ़, सीमा, भाषा आ (digital technology) अलग-अलग विषय नहि; ओ सभ (social reproduction) आ (agency)क परस्पर सम्बन्धित स्थल छथि। स्त्री-अनुभव केँ ज्ञान बनबैत समय दुइटा खतरा बराबर टारब आवश्यक अछि: एक दिस (patriarchal silence), दोसर दिस (romanticized) “(women’s voice)” जे (contradiction) आ (hierarchy) मेटा दैत अछि।

en.title: Mithila’s Parallel Feminist Perspective
en.summary: Mithila’s parallel feminist perspective is not a declaration of ancient glory but a method: listen to local sources, examine institutional power, do not essentialise experience, and keep the criteria of justice explicit. Within this perspective, Panji, marriage, family, song, art, labour, migration, flood, border, language and digital technology are not separate topics; they are interconnected sites of social reproduction and agency. In turning women’s experience into knowledge, two dangers must be avoided equally: on one side patriarchal silence, and on the other a romanticised “women’s voice” that erases contradiction and hierarchy.
